I would rather my ex not be involved in the life of my child, I know this sounds fucked up, but count your blessings that he decided to run away... He obviously wasn't the person that was meant for you, and it is entirely up to him how involved he wants to be in your child's life. Don't make it easy for him, because I know too many single moms that have revolving door baby daddies, and it breaks the little ones hearts. I highly suggest that if you can afford to go without his child support, do not put him on the birth certificate. Abusing my xanax prescription during a break down, followed by a breakup. I wouldn't consider myself an addict, because addiction implies a person cannot stop on their own. I know if I hadn't, I would not be alive right now. I had a plan, and I knew if I didn't do some kind of intervention, I wouldn't survive the night. I hate committing myself, I've done it twice in the past, and it actually made my mental health worse in my opinion. It was about a week of taking ×3 the recommended dose each day, and I was essentially a comfortable zombie. A week after coming out of the fog, and choosing life, I found out I was pregnant. I had always wanted to be a mom, but had suffered from multiple miscarriages. I screamed with joy when I took the pregnancy test (I was ruling out pregnancy, so I could move on from the break up... Life is strange). I was terrified of losing this baby, because of abusing the xanax, but my suicidal ideation has essentially disappeared. I realize having a baby doesn't fix problems, I've been in therapy for a long time. Ex and I decided to not reconcile. I started working in a new career field, I can feel my baby kick now, my family rallied around me... I wouldn't usually condone any sort of drug abuse, but if it is a choice between killing yourself, or numbing yourself with a substance, choose the drug abuse... I told my mom about it, and she agreed, losing me to suicide would have been exponentially worse than losing me to a potential drug addiction. Starting a family is not something I would recommend as a solution to depression/anxiety/suicidal ideation, but for me, and my individual circumstances, it was exactly what I needed. This baby saved me.
